clue.text: Limit school subject being taken by fundamentalist?

parts.note: RE is religious education, a subject in British schools
a fundamentalist holds to a strict reading of doctrine

explanation.surface: A rule capping how much religious teaching a hardline believer may take on.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a standard subject in British schools; the question mark flags that a fundamentalist being 'strict' is a loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to confine or curb it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: One very intimate penetrating soldiers, one of many in a cell

definitions.text: one of many in a cell

indicators.note: the intimate piece pierces the soldiers piece and sits within it

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
I is the Roman numeral for one
a bosom friend is a very close one

explanation.surface: A lover gets among the troops, one of many in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests a prison, but it is the biological unit.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny particle that builds proteins occurs in large numbers within every living cell.

clue.text: Fish immediately going into that cold water

indicators.note: the immediately piece enters the fish piece

parts.note: a smelt is a small fish
now means at once

explanation.surface: A fish dives at once into icy water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water running off when snow thaws is chilly by nature.

clue.text: Viceroy always entertains this member of top family

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters within it, as a host holds guests

explanation.surface: A colonial governor always hosts a member of the ruling house.
explanation.definitionFit: A person belonging to the monarch's household is part of the top family in the land.

clue.text: Builder's beginning to get stuck into nasty terrace, transforming London thoroughfare

indicators.note: the letter is lodged inside the rearranged letters
the letters of the two words are transformed into a new order
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A builder makes a start on an ugly terrace and turns it into a famous road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transforming' rearranges NASTYTERRACE, and B, the beginning of 'Builder's', is 'stuck into' it. The answer is the Soho street famed for sixties fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: This Soho shopping street was the heart of Swinging London fashion, a city thoroughfare.

clue.text: Annual meeting without English is showing a type of prejudice

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the meeting's letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: AGM is the abbreviation for annual general meeting
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company's yearly gathering, with no English present, reveals bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but here is the old sense 'outside', so the meeting goes round the rest rather than losing English.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrimination against people because of how old they are is a recognised form of prejudice.

clue.text: Lord again replaced chandelier

indicators.note: the letters are placed again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nobleman swaps out his light fitting once more.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an ornate branched candlestick or light holder, a kind of chandelier.

clue.text: Terribly violent, no end, feeling great passion

indicators.note: done terribly means done badly, so the letters are mixed up
the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone fiercely violent without limit, consumed by passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' drops the T of 'violent', and 'Terribly' rearranges the remaining VIOLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be smitten with someone is to feel strong romantic passion.

clue.text: With-it girl appearing in Italian city

parts.note: mod means modern and fashionable
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fashionable young woman turns up in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: A mod was a 1960s style-conscious British youth, so 'with-it'.
explanation.definitionFit: This city in Emilia-Romagna, home of balsamic vinegar, is in northern Italy.

clue.text: Sort of practical joke? Jolly mistake on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters of the two words are read backwards

parts.note: a jolly is a party or outing
a boob is a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a cheerful blunder might count as a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' looks like 'thinking it over' but turns PARTYBOOB round. 'Jolly' is a noun here, a party, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealed trap set to catch the unwary is one kind of prank, though it can be deadly, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Males departed, sailing around in old ship

indicators.note: the letters move around freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The men have left, cruising about in a vintage vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat driven by steam-powered wheels on its sides is a vessel of a bygone age.

clue.text: Was in charge and took control after game

indicators.note: the control piece comes after the game piece, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: RU is rugby union
led means took charge or guided

explanation.surface: Someone captained the side and seized command once the match ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch or leader who governed was in charge, a past-tense verb match.

clue.text: Thus male needs another name, edging off in foreign country

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: one edge of the word is taken away, here its final letter

parts.note: an alias is an assumed name

explanation.surface: A man needs an assumed identity to slip away abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edging off' strips the last letter from ALIAS, leaving ALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This East African nation on the Horn of Africa is a foreign country to the British setter.

clue.text: Singer put on old vehicle

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A vocalist is loaded aboard an ancient vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish folk-pop performer of the 1960s is a well-known vocalist.

clue.text: Fellow's rhymes for yesteryear's pop song

definitions.meaning: two words that end in -ellow and so rhyme with fellow, one meaning soft and ripe, the other a colour
a 1966 hit single by the singer at 13-across

explanation.surface: A chap's rhyming words make up an old chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1966 hit links to 13-across, its singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words both rhyme with fellow, and together they are the title of a sixties pop record.

clue.text: Upper-class cheat, 7 repeatedly, not quite a paragon, a self-absorbed 23

parts.note: the answer to 7-down ends in a word that in tennis means zero, the letter O, used twice
to rob is to cheat or swindle
the answer to 7-down ends in a word that in tennis means zero, the letter O, used twice

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a rose is a paragon, the finest of its kind

explanation.surface: A posh fraud, smitten twice over and nearly perfect, is a self-obsessed serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is 7-down, whose love is O, here used twice. 'Not quite' drops the E from ROSE. 23 is 23-down.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient symbol shows a serpent swallowing its own tail, so it is literally absorbed in itself.

clue.text: Wife is hard with inclination to get a series of desirable items

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a list is a tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A wife is determined to acquire a run of covetable things.
explanation.definitionFit: A rundown of things one wants to have is a catalogue of desired items.

clue.text: Excited and hugging one chum

indicators.note: the word and wraps around the other pieces as if hugging them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone gets thrilled while embracing a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link word but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lively and full of spirit is close in sense to being stirred up.

clue.text: Patriot's tone quivering when making solemn avowal

indicators.note: something quivering trembles and shakes, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A patriot's voice trembles as he swears an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quivering' shuffles the twelve letters of PATRIOTSTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn declaration or affirmation of something is an avowal, the formal sense of the word.

clue.text: Yearned to be married, having lost first husband

indicators.note: something lost has gone, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to get hitched is to marry

indicators.note: the first of the word husband means its opening letter only

explanation.surface: A woman longed to wed, having lost her first spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to have an itch for it, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Novelist who proceeds at a slow pace?

definitions.meaning: Eric ..., the English writer of spy thrillers

definitions.text: who proceeds at a slow pace?
definitions.meaning: someone who strolls along in a leisurely way

explanation.surface: A writer who is a slow walker.
explanation.definitionFit: The thriller writer's surname also names someone who walks at an easy, unhurried pace.

clue.text: Mum's got stuck in a bit of furniture — wild but likely to calm down?

definitions.text: wild but likely to calm down?

indicators.note: the mother piece is lodged inside the furniture piece

parts.note: a table is an item of furniture
ma is a word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother is wedged in a table, frantic but probably soon settled.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild creature that can be domesticated is one that may be calmed and trained.

clue.text: Thames meanders round a part of the capital

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the a
a river that meanders winds about, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: London's river winds its way round a district of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meanders' turns THAMES into ESTHAM, which goes 'round' A after its first letter. The answer is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The district in the London borough of Newham is one area of the British capital.

clue.text: Tempter appearing in lascivious nakedness

indicators.note: the letters show up within the two words

explanation.surface: The tempter turns up in lustful nudity, as in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the serpent tempts Eve to eat the forbidden fruit.

clue.text: Foreign money must be robust, right?

parts.note: hale means healthy and robust

explanation.surface: A demand that a currency be strong, with a questioning tag.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Czech coin, a hundredth of a koruna, is a unit of foreign currency.

clue.text: Tiny fellow, one tickling the ivories, not one banging drums

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the small boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

indicators.note: not, with the following one, says an I (the figure one) is dropped from the keyboard player

parts.note: tickling the ivories is playing the piano, so this is a pianist

explanation.surface: A little man plays the piano rather than thumping drums.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'one' after 'not' does double duty: 'not one' removes an I from PIANIST and 'one banging drums' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestral player of the kettledrums is a percussionist who strikes them.

clue.text: Coercion to put on finer attire around university

indicators.note: the dressing-up piece wraps around the university letter

parts.note: to dress up is to put on smart clothes

explanation.surface: Students are pressured to dress smartly on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Threats or pressure used to force someone to act is compulsion, a near synonym.

clue.text: A left-winger's to remain inside, taken into custody

indicators.note: the remaining piece sits inside the left-winger piece

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
to rest is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: A socialist must stay indoors after being detained.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held by police after being seized is in custody, the exact sense.
